rationale:
The reviewed tests adequately check `requirements.sdk.outlines.selection`.

**Obligations and test mapping**

- **Resolving a selector from the root against the retained outline.**
  - `rust_items_attach_documentation_and_preserve_structural_hashes` selects every outline item by its selector. It asserts that the text equals the item's span and that the structural hash matches.
  - `markdown_heading_levels_resolve_encoded_duplicates_and_anonymous_items` resolves percent-encoded names, `#N` duplicates and anonymous `block@` and `section@` selectors.
  - `css_duplicate_names_are_numbered_after_normalization_within_each_parent` and `unicode_spans_use_bytes_and_whitespace_only_lines_create_no_items` cover further resolution cases.
  - In the markdown test, `second.select(main)` is called on an already-selected handle. It resolves from the file root, not from the selected item.
  - The empty selector is covered by `selected.select("")` in `selected_contents_outlive_handles_and_later_file_edits`.

- **Another owned `OutlineContent` that shares the snapshot.**
  - The rust and markdown tests assert `std::ptr::eq(function.outline(), contents.outline())`, so the outline is shared.
  - `selected_contents_outlive_handles_and_later_file_edits` checks `id()` and `text()` on the selected content.

- **Sharing the fingerprinting rules.** `explicit_languages_share_configuration_and_retain_their_scheme` selects `part[selected]` from content built with a custom language. It asserts that the selected item keeps the `custom-v2` scheme and that its fingerprint matches the one from the path-loaded handle. It also asserts that a `custom-v3` language gives a different fingerprint for the same hash. The `fingerprint_scheme()` assertions in `selected_contents_outlive_handles_and_later_file_edits` add to this.

- **No additional file read, and still usable after the original handle is dropped.** In `selected_contents_outlive_handles_and_later_file_edits`, the file handle is dropped and the file is then rewritten on disk. The earlier selection keeps its text and fingerprint. `selected.select("")` still returns the original root text `first\nsecond\n`, so selection did not re-read the file. In the same test, `from_id` fails after the edit, which shows the file really changed.

- **Selector syntax, including interchangeable identical plain-text lines.**
  - `unknown_extensions_keep_nonblank_lines_and_content_selectors` selects a duplicated `alpha` line by its selector.
  - `ambiguous_items_are_errors_except_for_identical_plain_text_lines` asserts that two `same` lines share one selector and that selecting it succeeds.
  - The same test shows that a `line` item with differing hashes is still reported as ambiguous.

- **Errors for invalid, missing and ambiguous selections.**
  - `missing_file_and_invalid_selections_are_errors` asserts errors for the malformed selector `fn[` and the missing selector `fn[absent]`.
  - `ambiguous_items_are_errors_except_for_identical_plain_text_lines` asserts an error containing "ambiguous" for duplicate `part[same]` items and for `line` items with differing hashes.
  - `css_duplicate_names_are_numbered_after_normalization_within_each_parent` asserts that the unnumbered `rule[a%20b]` is an error.

- **`text()` is the original selected text, before redaction.** `formatted_contents_redact_credentials_while_retaining_raw_text_and_spans` selects a line containing a token. It asserts that `selected.text()` keeps the raw token and that `format()` redacts it.

**Delegated obligations.** The details of selector syntax, such as the twelve-digit hash and percent-encoding rules, belong to `requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax`. The error format belongs to `requirements.sdk.outlines.errors`. Both are cited context and are also exercised incidentally here.

I found no plausible requirement-violating behavior that these tests would accept.

text: :::{req} selection
`OutlineContent::select` resolves a selector from the file's root against the
retained outline. It returns another owned `OutlineContent` for that item,
sharing the original source snapshot and fingerprinting rules. Selection
performs no additional file read and remains usable after the original handle
is dropped. Resolution follows
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax`, including its rule that
identical plain-text lines are interchangeable. Invalid, missing, or ambiguous
selections return an error under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.errors`.
```rust,ignore
impl OutlineContent {
/// Select an item from this retained file snapshot.
pub fn select(&self, selector: &str) -> Result<Self, OutlineError>;
/// Address of the selected item.
pub fn id(&self) -> &OutlineData;
/// Original selected text, including attached source, before redaction.
pub fn text(&self) -> &str;
:::{req} selector_syntax
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
:::{req} errors
The outline API makes a best effort to recover from parse errors.
File-read and unrecoverable parsing failures return errors, distinct from
successful contents for an empty file. Selecting a language commits to that
language's parsing rules.
A malformed selector, a missing item, or an ambiguity not permitted by
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax` also returns an error.
